hypothesis: Database connection exhaustion caused by payroll batch workers scaling up to maximum threads and consuming most PostgreSQL connections, leading to portal API timeouts. ConnectionPoolPressure and TooManyConnections errors indicate the database reached its connection limit. WorkerPoolScaleUp and WorkerPoolAtMaximum warnings show the batch workers were running at full capacity. The payroll‑portal API depends on the same database, so exhaustion would affect it. Historical RCAs and incidents consistently link payroll batch runs to portal timeouts. The timing of the errors aligns with the start of the payroll batch run.

Misconfiguration of the payroll‑app connection pool caused connections to be held longer than necessary, leading to exhaustion. Connection timeouts and TooManyConnections errors point to a shortage of available connections. ConnectionPoolPressure warnings suggest the pool was under stress. The payroll‑portal API depends on the same database, so a pool misconfiguration would affect it. Historical incidents show similar symptoms during payroll runs, which could be due to pool settings.

Unclosed database sessions in the payment retry-handler code caused connection pool exhaustion. ConnectionTimeout errors and ConnectionPoolPressure warnings indicate pool exhaustion Retry-handler change was deployed immediately before the first errors Past RCA (RCA-2025-00114) identified the same issue in a previous release

The database connection pool was insufficient for the load, leading to exhaustion independent of code changes. ConnectionTimeout and ConnectionPoolPressure warnings are consistent with pool exhaustion The retry-handler change may have increased load but not necessarily caused unclosed sessions Similar symptoms were observed in past incidents during peak traffic

Cross‑region latency to the session lock store caused lock acquisition failures and session conflicts during the region failover. Region failover moved traffic to eu-central-1 while the lock store remained in eu-west-1, creating high round‑trip times. Cross‑region latency warnings precede the lock failures, indicating network delay. Lock acquisition failures and session conflicts are typical symptoms of delayed lock release due to latency. The portal’s session lock store is a dedicated Redis instance, as shown in the CMDB. The timing of the errors aligns with the failover event.

The portal-session-lock-redis instance was overloaded or misconfigured, leading to high latency and lock contention independent of the region failover. LockAcquisitionFailure and SessionConflict errors are consistent with a slow or overloaded lock store. Cross‑region latency warnings could be a symptom of an overloaded Redis instance rather than network delay. The CMDB indicates a dedicated Redis cache for session locks, which could be experiencing resource pressure. The errors began shortly after the region failover, but the failover itself may have increased load on the lock store. No evidence of a recent change to the lock store configuration is present in the ledger.
